rules: Give the viewer a concrete question: whether a delivery will arrive before the bridge folds, whether a decoy will fool the wrong pursuer, or whether two characters realize they are solving opposite halves of the same problem.
Show what success and failure look like.
Alternate action with short opportunities to understand new information.
Narrow the available choices as the film proceeds.
A time limit should change decisions.
A clock that never affects behavior is decoration.
An apparent escape should expose a meaningful cost or reveal a new relationship.
Keep geography legible; uncertainty about what happens next is useful, confusion about where everyone stands usually is not.
Let sound anticipate a threat only when the source and payoff make sense.
contract_note: Suspense comes from uncertainty with understandable consequences, not merely dark music or a slowly opening door.
